course.title: Hydraulic Engineering
course.department: Department of Civil Engineering, CHRIST (Deemed to be University), Kengeri Campus
course.prereqs: Engineering Physics, Engineering Mathematics, Fluid Mechanics (CE204)

textbooks.cite: P. N. Modi and S. M. Seth, 'Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics Including Hydraulics Machines', Standard Book House, New Delhi, 22nd ed., 2022.
R. K. Bansal, 'A Textbook of Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Machines', Laxmi Publications, New Delhi, 10th ed., 2021.
Ven Te Chow, 'Open-Channel Hydraulics', McGraw-Hill, New York (reprinted by Blackburn Press), 1959/2009.

references.cite: K. Subramanya, 'Flow in Open Channels', McGraw-Hill Education (India), 5th ed., 2019.
M. Hanif Chaudhry, 'Open-Channel Flow', Springer, 2nd ed., 2008.
H. K. Versteeg and W. Malalasekera, 'An Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics: The Finite Volume Method', Pearson, 2nd ed., 2007.
US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), 'HEC-RAS Hydraulic Reference Manual', Version 6.5, Davis, CA, 2024.

units.title: Boundary Layer Theory
units.syllabus: Physical concepts of boundary layer; laminar and turbulent boundary layer; boundary layer thickness; displacement, momentum and energy thickness; boundary layer over flat plate; von Kármán momentum integral equation; skin friction drag and boundary layer separation; cavitation.

units.title: Open Channel Flow
units.syllabus: Difference between pipe and open channel flow; types of open channels and geometric elements; Chezy and Manning equations; most economical channel sections (rectangular, trapezoidal, triangular); specific energy concept and critical depth; channel transitions and critical flow analysis; hydraulic jump: types, characteristics and energy dissipation; GVF and RVF overview.

units.title: Impact of Jets
units.syllabus: Dynamic action of fluid jet; impulse-momentum principle; force exerted on stationary flat and curved plates (normal and inclined); force on moving flat and curved plates; series of vanes; jet propulsion of ships; work done, power and hydraulic efficiency of jet action.

units.title: Hydraulic Machines: Turbines and Pumps
units.syllabus: Classification of hydraulic machines; impulse turbines (Pelton wheel): component parts, velocity triangles, work done, efficiency, design principles; reaction turbines (Francis and Kaplan): working principles, velocity diagrams, draft tube theory, cavitation; centrifugal pumps: working principle, work done, manometric head, efficiencies, minimum starting speed, multistage pumps, specific speed, cavitation.

units.title: Computational Hydraulics & 2D Hydrodynamic Modeling
units.syllabus: Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) in hydraulic engineering; governing equations: Navier-Stokes and shallow water equations (SWE); 2D hydrodynamic modeling of open channels; grid generation and boundary conditions; Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) stability criterion; SimFlow/OpenFOAM CFD modeling of hydraulic structures; HEC-RAS 2D unsteady flow modeling; inundation mapping, depth and velocity validation.

pages.title: Software setup
pages.hook: Install HEC-RAS 2D and SimFlow CFD before starting the computational lab track.

pages.title: Project (PBL)
pages.hook: Design a flood diversion channel, spillway energy dissipator, and 2D hydraulic simulation model.

pages.title: Assessment
pages.hook: Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA), mid-term examinations, end-semester evaluation, and lab rubrics.

pages.title: References
pages.hook: Standard textbooks, design handbooks, USACE engineering manuals, and IS codes.

labs.title: Verification of Boundary Layer Velocity Profiles
labs.goal: Measure laminar and turbulent boundary layer profiles and compute displacement and momentum thicknesses.

labs.title: Flow Visualization & Boundary Layer Separation
labs.goal: Observe flow separation past bluff bodies, airfoils and adverse pressure gradients in a flow channel.

labs.title: Cavitation Inception in a Venturi / Orifice
labs.goal: Determine critical pressure drop, Thoma cavitation factor, and noise/vibration inception in restricted conduit flow.

labs.title: Uniform Flow & Manning's Roughness Determination
labs.goal: Measure normal depth at varying discharges in a tilting flume and calculate Manning's n and Chezy's C.

labs.title: Specific Energy & Critical Depth Verification
labs.goal: Construct specific energy curve experimentally and verify critical depth over a broad-crested weir and hump.

labs.title: Hydraulic Jump & Energy Dissipation
labs.goal: Form hydraulic jumps in a laboratory flume, measure conjugate depths, and compare head loss against Bélanger's equation.

labs.title: Gradually Varied Flow (GVF) Water Surface Profiles
labs.goal: Compute and measure M1 and M2 backwater profiles using the Standard Step Method and compare with HEC-RAS 1D.

labs.title: Impact of Jet on Flat & Curved Vanes
labs.goal: Measure hydrodynamic impact force exerted by water jet on stationary flat plate, hemispherical cup and 60° curved vane.

labs.title: Momentum Analysis of Moving Vanes & Series of Vanes
labs.goal: Determine mechanical power and hydrodynamic efficiency of moving vane assembly and compare with momentum theory.

labs.title: Performance Characteristics of Pelton Turbine
labs.goal: Operate a Pelton wheel test rig at constant head and variable speed; plot unit power, unit speed and efficiency curves.

labs.title: Performance Characteristics of Francis / Kaplan Turbine
labs.goal: Determine operating characteristics and efficiency curves of reaction turbine at various guide vane openings.

labs.title: Operating Characteristics of Centrifugal Pump
labs.goal: Measure total head, flow rate and shaft power; establish H-Q curve, efficiency curve, and best efficiency point (BEP).

labs.title: HEC-RAS 2D Mesh Generation & Terrain Setup
labs.goal: Create a 2D computation mesh in RAS Mapper, enforce breaklines along channel banks, and set Manning n regions.

labs.title: HEC-RAS 2D Unsteady Flow & Flood Inundation
labs.goal: Simulate unsteady hydrograph routing through a 2D channel; check CFL condition and map maximum flood inundation.

labs.title: SimFlow/OpenFOAM CFD Modeling of Hydraulic Structure
labs.goal: Set up 2D/3D numerical simulation of flow over a spillway or through a sluice gate and validate free-surface profile.

sessions.title: Physical Concepts of Boundary Layer Theory
sessions.hook: Why does a fluid flow adhere completely to solid boundaries, creating a microscopic shear zone that dictates the drag on submarines and river channels?
outcomes: State the no-slip condition and explain why boundary layers form on solid walls
Identify the nominal boundary layer thickness delta_0.99 where u = 0.99 U_inf
Calculate local Reynolds number Re_x and determine laminar to turbulent transition point
sessions.keywords: no-slip condition Prandtl hypothesis viscous flow transition Reynolds number

sessions.title: Boundary Layer Thickness Definitions
sessions.hook: How much does a boundary layer displace the external streamlines outward, and what fraction of fluid momentum is lost to wall friction?
outcomes: Define and compute displacement thickness delta* as the outward shift of outer streamlines
Calculate momentum thickness theta and link it directly to total skin friction drag
Evaluate the shape factor H = delta* / theta to assess velocity profile fullness
sessions.keywords: displacement thickness momentum thickness energy thickness shape factor H

sessions.title: Von Kármán Momentum Integral Equation
sessions.hook: How can an integral momentum balance across a simple rectangular control volume solve boundary layer growth without solving full Navier-Stokes equations?
outcomes: Explain the Von Kármán momentum integral equation tau_0 = rho * U^2 * d(theta)/dx
Apply wall and outer-edge boundary conditions to solve for velocity profile shape
Calculate laminar boundary layer thickness and local skin friction using Blasius solutions
sessions.keywords: Von Kármán equation momentum integral wall shear stress shear velocity

sessions.title: Laminar Boundary Layer on a Flat Plate
sessions.hook: Why does the boundary layer thickness grow precisely as the square root of distance (√x) in laminar flow?
outcomes: Apply the 1/7th power law and Blasius equations to laminar and turbulent boundary layers
Explain why turbulent boundary layer thickness grows as x^(4/5) compared to laminar x^(1/2)
Calculate total skin friction drag force on submerged plates in turbulent flow
sessions.keywords: Blasius solution cubic profile laminar growth local skin friction

sessions.title: Turbulent Boundary Layer on a Flat Plate
sessions.hook: Why does turbulence cause a boundary layer to expand five times thicker than laminar flow, yet drastically resist flow separation?
outcomes: Explain why a laminar sublayer delta' = 11.6 * nu / u_* persists even inside turbulent flow
Compute shear velocity u_* = sqrt(tau_0 / rho) from bed shear stress
Classify boundaries into hydrodynamically smooth, transitional, or rough using Nikuradse's criteria
sessions.keywords: 1/7th power law turbulent boundary layer law of the wall eddy viscosity

sessions.title: Laminar Sublayer & Boundary Roughness
sessions.hook: Can a microscopically rough concrete surface behave as hydrodynamically glass-smooth under low flow velocities?
outcomes: Explain how an adverse pressure gradient (dp/dx > 0) causes flow deceleration and boundary layer separation
Identify the separation point where wall shear stress vanishes (tau_0 = 0)
Differentiate skin friction drag from form (pressure) drag and evaluate separation control methods
sessions.keywords: laminar sublayer Nikuradse roughness hydrodynamically smooth rough boundary

sessions.title: Local and Average Skin Friction Drag
sessions.hook: How do naval architects and hydraulic flume designers compute the exact friction drag force acting along submerged surfaces?
sessions.keywords: skin friction coefficient total drag force mixed boundary layer wetted area

sessions.title: Boundary Layer Separation & Pressure Gradients
sessions.hook: What causes fluid flow to suddenly detach from a spillway crest or bridge pier, generating devastating vortex shedding and cavitation?
sessions.keywords: boundary layer separation adverse pressure gradient inflection point wake drag

sessions.title: Boundary Layer Control Methods & Civil Applications
sessions.hook: How do hydraulic engineers inject microscopic air bubbles into high-head spillway shoots to suppress cavitation damage completely?
sessions.keywords: boundary layer control suction and blowing vortex generators aeration slots

sessions.title: Introduction to Free Surface Flow & Channel Geometry
sessions.hook: Why does the presence of a free surface at constant atmospheric pressure make open channel hydraulics far richer and more complex than closed pipe flow?
outcomes: Explain why the gauge pressure at the free water surface is always zero
Compute wetted area A, perimeter P, hydraulic radius R, and hydraulic depth D
Distinguish steady vs unsteady and uniform vs varied channel flows
sessions.keywords: geometric elements hydraulic radius hydraulic depth open channel flow

sessions.title: Velocity Distribution & Kinetic Energy / Momentum Factors
sessions.hook: Why is the point of maximum velocity in an open channel depressed 5% to 25% below the free surface rather than right at the top?
outcomes: Identify where maximum velocity occurs and explain the velocity dip
Calculate mean velocity V using IS:1192 0.6y single-point and 0.2y/0.8y two-point standards
Apply the Coriolis factor α and Boussinesq factor β to energy and momentum equations
sessions.keywords: velocity distribution Coriolis factor α Boussinesq factor β streamline curvature

sessions.title: Uniform Flow: Chezy's & Manning's Equations
sessions.hook: How did Robert Manning formulate an empirical equation in 1889 that remains the supreme global standard for river and canal design today?
outcomes: Explain how downslope gravity pull balances bed shear friction in uniform flow
Show why opposing hydrostatic load triangles cancel out
Calculate discharge using Manning's equation and composite roughness using Cowan's method
sessions.keywords: Manning equation Chezy formula roughness coefficient n Cowan method

sessions.title: Most Economical (Hydraulically Efficient) Sections
sessions.hook: For a fixed volume of excavation and lining material, what exact mathematical geometry delivers the highest possible discharge?
outcomes: State the geometric conditions for economical rectangular and trapezoidal sections
Prove why b = 2y and R = y/2 minimizes concrete lining perimeter
Explain why a circular pipe achieves peak discharge before it is 100% full
sessions.keywords: hydraulically efficient section half-hexagon minimum wetted perimeter maximum discharge

sessions.title: Computation of Normal Depth & Uniform Flow
sessions.hook: How do engineers quickly solve the non-linear implicit Manning equation for water depth without manual trial and error?
outcomes: Explain why normal depth is implicit in Manning's equation
Apply the Bisection and Newton-Raphson methods to solve for normal depth yn
Use Excel Goal Seek or Python to calculate uniform flow depth
sessions.keywords: normal depth y0 Newton-Raphson section factor tractive force

sessions.title: Specific Energy and Critical Flow
sessions.hook: One flow, two possible depths: which one does the channel choose, and why does the depth in the middle matter?
outcomes: Explain why the same flow can be deep and slow or shallow and fast
Find the critical depth and the minimum specific energy for a rectangular channel
Use the Froude number to say whether ripples can travel upstream
sessions.keywords: specific energy critical depth Froude number alternate depths

sessions.title: Channel Transitions: Humps and Narrowings
sessions.hook: Why does the water surface dip over a bump on the bed in calm flow, and rise in fast flow?
outcomes: Predict whether water surface rises or dips over bed steps in sub- and supercritical flow
Calculate the maximum step height dz_max before channel choking occurs
Find the minimum contracted throat width b_min that avoids afflux backwater
sessions.keywords: channel transition bed hump width contraction choking condition

sessions.title: The Hydraulic Jump
sessions.hook: Why is there a wall of white water below every spillway, and where does the energy go?
outcomes: Find the depth after a jump, the energy lost and the length for a rectangular channel
Explain why momentum, not energy, is used across a jump
Say what happens to the jump when the tailwater is too low or too high
sessions.keywords: hydraulic jump Bélanger equation energy dissipation stilling basin

sessions.title: Gradually Varied Flow (GVF) & Surface Profiles
sessions.hook: How do river engineers accurately predict how many kilometers upstream a newly constructed reservoir will submerge farm lands?
outcomes: Explain the GVF governing equation dy/dx = (S0 - Sf)/(1 - Fr^2)
Classify the 12 water surface profiles across Mild, Steep, Critical, Horizontal, and Adverse slopes
Compute backwater curve reach lengths using the Direct Step Method
sessions.keywords: gradually varied flow backwater curve M1 profile Direct Step Method

sessions.title: Impulse-Momentum Principle & Jet Hydrodynamics
sessions.hook: How much dynamic force can a 50 mm jet of water exert when blasted at 30 meters per second against a solid barrier?
outcomes: Apply the impulse-momentum principle to calculate dynamic thrust of fluid jets
Compute the impact force F_x = rho * a * V^2 on a fixed vertical flat plate
Explain why impact force quadruples when jet velocity is doubled
sessions.keywords: impulse-momentum jet hydrodynamics momentum flux nozzle coefficient

sessions.title: Force of Jet on Stationary Flat Plates
sessions.hook: When a high-speed jet strikes an inclined plate, how is the incoming water stream mathematically divided into forward and backward flows?

Compute the division of discharge into forward (Q_1) and backward (Q_2) streams

sessions.title: Force of Jet on Stationary Curved Vanes
sessions.hook: Why does curving a plate into a 180° hemispherical bucket precisely double the force exerted by an impinging water jet?

Prove why a 180-degree hemispherical cup experiences exactly twice the force of a flat plate (F = 2 rho a V^2)
Evaluate tangential entry curved vanes and resolve dynamic reaction forces

sessions.title: Force of Jet on Moving Flat Plates
sessions.hook: Why can a series of flat plates on a rotating wheel reach an efficiency of 50%, while a single moving plate can never exceed 29.6%?
outcomes: Distinguish mass flow striking a single moving plate rho * a * (V - u) from a series of plates on a wheel rho * a * V
Prove why the theoretical maximum efficiency of a single moving plate is 29.6% at u = V/3
Prove why a series of flat vanes on a wheel achieves a maximum efficiency of 50% at u = V/2
sessions.keywords: moving flat plate series of plates work done maximum efficiency

sessions.title: Force of Jet on Moving Curved Vanes
sessions.hook: Under what kinematic conditions can a series of curved vanes extract nearly 100% of the kinetic energy from a moving water jet?

Calculate relative velocity V_r and blade speed u for shockless tangential entry
Evaluate whirl velocities V_w and calculate runner power and hydraulic efficiency
sessions.keywords: moving curved vane wheel periphery runner power optimum speed ratio

sessions.title: Jet Striking a Series of Radial Vanes

sessions.title: Dynamic Velocity Triangles at Inlet and Outlet

Explain why radial discharge (V_w2 = 0) minimizes lost exit kinetic energy
